{"status":"ok","message-type":"work-list","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"facets":{},"total-results":12744052,"items":[{"abstract":"Fine-tuning large-scale neural networks for specific tasks often requires significant computational power and memory, making it an expensive and resource-intensive process. To address this issue, Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods have been introduced, enabling adaptation with a reduced number of trainable parameters. Among these techniques, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has gained widespread recognition for its efficiency and ease of integration. This survey provides a thorough exploration of LoRA, covering its mathematical principles, implementation techniques, and real-world applications. By comparing LoRA to traditional full fine-tuning and other PEFT methods, we highlight its ability to maintain strong performance while significantly cutting down on computational overhead. Empirical evaluations across various NLP benchmarks further demonstrate its effectiveness in reducing memory consumption without sacrificing accuracy. Beyond its advantages, we also examine the challenges associated with LoRA, such as rank selection sensitivity, compatibility with different model architectures, and potential hardware optimizations. Additionally, we discuss promising future directions, including hybrid fine-tuning strategies, dynamic rank adjustment, and expansion into multi-modal learning. By enabling more efficient adaptation of complex models, LoRA represents a crucial advancement in scalable fine-tuning. This survey aims to serve as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners looking to leverage LoRA for optimized model training across diverse applications.","DOI":"10.36227/techrxiv.174015835.57150536/v1","type":"posted-content","is-referenced-by-count":1,"title":["Revolutionizing Large Model Fine-Tuning: The Role of LoRA in Parameter-Efficient Adaptation"],"author":[{"ORCID":"https://orcid.org/0009-0004-1264-1902","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Jianhong","family":"Shun","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Chang","family":"Zheng","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2025,2,21]]},"URL":"https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.174015835.57150536/v1"},{"abstract":"Abstract

Source code optimization enables developers to enhance programs at the human-computer interaction level, thereby improving development efficiency and product quality. With the rise of large language models (LLMs), fine-tuning and prompting have become mainstream solutions for this task. However, both approaches present challenges: fine-tuning is resource-intensive due to the exponential growth in the scale of LLMs, whereas prompting, although resource-efficient, struggles to generate high-quality optimized programs. In this paper, we present CodeOPT, a LoRA-driven approach for fine-tuning LLMs to optimize C/C++ code. Instead of fine-tuning all LLM parameters, CodeOPT leverages LoRA to fine-tune only an optimization adapter, significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters. Additionally, we incorporate prior optimization knowledge during fine-tuning and introduce optimization-based instruction fine-tuning, enabling LLMs to effectively learn from external knowledge sources to improve program optimization. To evaluate the effectiveness of CodeOPT, we benchmarked it against several baselines on challenging programming tasks from different code completion platforms. Experimental results demonstrate that CodeOPT outperforms all baselines, including the state-of-the-art, while keeping modifications to the original program minimal.

Retrieval"],"is-referenced-by-count":1,"URL":"https://doi.org/10.1145/3711542.3711579","type":"proceedings-article"},{"abstract":"Large Language Models (LLMs) perform well in many text classification tasks, such as sentiment analysis, spam detection, and topic classification. However, adapting large language models to downstream tasks via full-parameter fine-tuning often requires significant computing power and GPU memory, resulting in high training costs, which is impractical for course assignments or resource-constrained scenarios. To address this issue, Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) has gradually become a popular approach. Its idea is to freeze most model parameters and train only a small number of additional parameters, thereby reducing training costs. This paper takes text classification as an example and begins with an introduction to fundamental concepts such as stochastic gradient descent, cross-entropy loss, and confusion matrices. It first reviews the technological evolution from traditional NLP models (such as bag-of-words, Naive Bayes, and N-grams) to word embeddings, Transformers, and ultimately large language models. Then, it focuses on the low-rank adaptation concept of LoRA and the 4-bit quantization training mechanism of QLoRA, analyzing their characteristics from the perspectives of parameter count, GPU memory consumption, and training stability. This paper also discusses key representation-level issues such as word segmentation methods (BPE, WordPiece, SentencePiece), Type/Token differentiation, vocabulary size, and sequence length, explaining how these factors affect the model's generalization ability. Overall, this paper aims to answer the question of "how to adapt large models to text classification tasks at a lower cost under limited resources," and provides a clearer theoretical framework and methodological approach for course learning and introductory research.","DOI":"10.54254/2755-2721/2026.gu34136","type":"journal-article","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Research on Efficient Fine-tuning of Large Language Model Parameters for Text Classification: A Review from Gradient Descent Basics to LoRA/QLoRA Methods"],"author":[{"given":"Tianyi","family":"Qu","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"Jiangsu University"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"container-title":["Applied and Computational Engineering"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,6,8]]},"URL":"https://doi.org/10.54254/2755-2721/2026.gu34136"},{"DOI":"10.7717/peerj.19919/fig-1","title":["Figure 1: Each pre-trained protein language model is fine-tuned on viral protein sequences ( x ) using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT)’s LoRA method."],"issued":{"date-parts":[[null]]},"is-referenced-by-count":1,"URL":"https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.19919/fig-1","type":"component"},{"abstract":"Abstract

Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on narrow task-specific datasets can induce broad behavioural misalignment — a phenomenon termed emergent misalignment. We present two studies of Domain Persona Capture (DPC). Study 1: Nine state-of-the-art LLMs (Llama-3.x, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2, Gemma-4) fine-tuned on 6,000 question–answer pairs derived from US Army doctrine using LoRA showed emergent misalignment rates of 83.8–100%, with the Gemma-4 26B MoE architecture showing substantially greater robustness. Study 2: Multimodal fine-tuning of Gemma-4 E2B and E4B revealed a novel dormant DPC phenomenon: multimodally fine-tuned models appeared moderately safe under text-only evaluation (EM 24–44%) but exhibited near-total misalignment (EM 99–100%) when any image — regardless of content — was provided at inference time. This visual anchoring effect creates a systematic blind spot in standard text-only safety evaluation frameworks.
